Chapter 7: Navigating Setbacks and Emotional Roadblocks
Even if you’ve set out with the best intentions, you’ll probably find that the road to a simpler life isn’t always a straight line. There are going to be bumps—sometimes practical, sometimes deeply emotional. Let’s talk through some of the most common challenges you might face, and how you can gently move forward when things get tough.
One thing that catches a lot of people off guard is the return of clutter. Life gets busy, routines slip, and suddenly, those tidy surfaces are covered again, and closets are bursting at the seams. But here’s the thing—this isn’t a sign that you’ve failed. Think of it like tending a garden. Weeds pop up, and you just need to give things a little attention now and then.
Emotional roadblocks can be even trickier. Sometimes, it isn’t about stuff at all—it’s about what that stuff represents. Maybe you feel guilty getting rid of gifts, or nostalgic about childhood souvenirs. Or perhaps you worry you’ll need those “just in case” supplies someday. These feelings are completely normal, and they deserve a little compassion.
So how do you handle these moments when they show up?
First, try adopting the “Memory, Not the Object” mindset. Remind yourself—your memories aren’t stored in things. If something is meaningful, snap a picture, or jot down a quick note about it. That way, you can honor the memory without hanging onto the physical item.
Next, give yourself permission to pause. If letting go of something feels too hard right now, it’s okay to set it aside. Come back to it when you feel ready—there’s no rush.
And be gentle with your self-talk. If you catch yourself being harsh or judgmental, try to swap that out for a little understanding. Change can be tough, and progress doesn’t always happen in a straight line.
Now, what if you’re not alone in this? Sometimes, family or housemates aren’t quite on board. That’s normal too. Open, respectful conversations can make a big difference. Talk about what matters to each of you, and try to move at a pace that feels right for everyone. Honoring each person’s attachments is key.
Another challenge? The urge to fill up empty spaces after decluttering. Maybe a room suddenly feels a little too bare, almost uncomfortable. That’s a totally natural reaction—after all, we’re often told that a “full” space is a cozy one. But what if you just sit with that emptiness for a bit? You might discover that open space brings a surprising sense of calm, and even possibility.
Remember, minimalism isn’t about getting it perfect. It’s about making choices, over and over, that line up with what matters most to you. Setbacks? They’re just reminders to return to those values, and keep moving forward at your own pace.
